s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with migration to the right lower quadrant
salient_findings: Abdominal pain migrating from the umbilicus to the right lower quadrant
Voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant
Leukocytosis with a white-cell count of 15,600/mL
Air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays
key_facts: Abdominal pain began 2 days prior to presentation
Pain migrated from the umbilicus to the right lower quadrant
Voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant
Minimal tenderness elsewhere in the abdomen
Air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays
Ultrasound assessment compatible with plastron appendicitis
Computed tomography showed a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen in the right lower quadrant

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Migratory pain to right lower quadrant, leukocytosis, and ultrasound findings compatible with plastron appendicitis

shortlist.label: Plastron appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Ultrasound assessment compatible with this condition and clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Small intestinal perforation
shortlist.why_kept: Air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays and computed tomography findings

shortlist.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and potential for similar symptoms to appendicitis

shortlist.label: Retrocecal appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Location of pain and potential for appendicitis in this area

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including migratory pain from the umbilicus to the right lower quadrant, elevated white-cell count, and imaging findings, are consistent with acute appendicitis. The ultrasound and computed tomography findings further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Plastron appendicitis
rejected.why: While the ultrasound suggested plastron appendicitis, this is not a commonly recognized medical term and the overall clinical picture is more consistent with acute appendicitis.

rejected.label: Small intestinal perforation
rejected.why: The absence of free air under the diaphragm on plain abdominal X-rays makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence in the case presentation to suggest Meckel's diverticulitis, such as a history of gastrointestinal bleeding or a known Meckel's diverticulum.

rejected.label: Retrocecal appendicitis
rejected.why: While possible, the clinical presentation and imaging findings do not specifically suggest a retrocecal location of the appendix.
